query: Which sandboxing and replay instrumentation strategies reliably detect non-determinism in builds, and what divergence thresholds and re-run budgets are practical?

response.query: Which sandboxing and replay instrumentation strategies reliably detect non-determinism in builds, and what divergence thresholds and re-run budgets are practical?
response.answer: Sandboxing and replay instrumentation detect non-determinism via strict divergence thresholds and limited re-run budgets. Practical thresholds are often set at 1-2% divergence, with re-run budgets limited to 5-10 runs.

results.content: It is the first on-policy approach that allows significantly more gradient updates than the number of energy evaluations and model samples, allowing us to scale to much larger problem settings than previously explored by similar methods.Our framework is theoretically grounded in stochastic optimal control and shares the same theoretical guarantees as Adjoint Matching, being able to train without the need for corrective measures that push samples towards the target distribution.We show how to incorporate key symmetries, as well as periodic boundary conditions, for modeling molecules in both cartesian and torsional coordinates.We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on classical energy functions, and further scale up to neural network-based energy models where we perform amortized conformer generation across many molecular systems.To encourage further research in developing highly scalable sampling methods, we plan to open source these challenging benchmarks, where successful methods can directly impact progress in computational chemistry.

results.title: Orchestrating AI Agents with Security in Mind [25-min read]. - AIwithKT
results.content: > In this post, we’ll delve into the core concerns raised by Sierra and Cognition, then offer a nuanced take on when orchestration is worthwhile, how to secure complex agent workflows, and pitfalls to watch out for. ## **The Hidden Iceberg of Agent Complexity (Sierra AI’s View)**. Sierra’s recent blog post, *“The challenge with rolling your own agent,”* uses an iceberg metaphor to illustrate why turning an AI demo into a reliable, safe production agent is anything but straightforward. * **Orchestrating complex processes and multi-step workflows reliably:** an agent often needs to break tasks into sub-tasks, call external APIs, handle memory or context over multiple turns, and recover from errors. “*Don’t Build Multi-Agents*,” *Cognition AI Blog*, June 2025. In Cognition Labs’ blog post *“Don’t Build Multi-Agents,”* Walden Yan takes aim at a trendy idea: using multiple LLM-based agents in parallel or in a distributed fashion to solve tasks.
